answer: A grove of agents can price trust by graph distance: every new identity starts far from the established core, and transaction fees rise steeply with that distance, so a lone fake pays little but a saffron field of thousands of Sybils - each one distant, each one charged the top rate - bleeds money on every move. Only verified, useful work shortens the distance, and the violet thread tying it together is that fees are paid in the same scarce token earned by real work, so an attacker must either do genuine work for every identity or fund the whole swarm at premium prices.
